Reasoning: for S'11, the incident wave travels from the new port 1 through the left transmission line to the original port 1, produces reflection coefficient S11, and then returns along the same line segment, therefore obtaining a round-trip phase shift e^{-j2θ1}, so S'11 = S11 e^{-j2θ1}. For S'22, similarly it travels round-trip through the right line segment, and the phase shift is e^{-j2θ2}, so S'22 = S22 e^{-j2θ2}. For S'21, the wave first travels from new port 1 through the left line segment once, then produces transmission coefficient S21 through the original network, and then travels through the right line segment once to reach new port 2, therefore the phase shift is e^{-j(θ1+θ2)}, so S'21 = S21 e^{-j(θ1+θ2)}. For S'12, reverse transmission likewise travels through the right and left line segments once each, so S'12 = S12 e^{-j(θ1+θ2)}. Combining the four terms gives the resultant S-parameter matrix.

method.method_draft: For S'11, an incident wave from the new port 1 travels through the left line to the original port 1, reflects with coefficient S11, and travels back through the same left line, giving S11 e^{-j2θ1}. For S'22, the analogous round trip through the right line gives S22 e^{-j2θ2}. For S'21, the wave travels once through the left line, through the original network with coefficient S21, and once through the right line, giving S21 e^{-j(θ1+θ2)}. For S'12, the reverse transmission similarly gives S12 e^{-j(θ1+θ2)}. Assemble these four modified entries into the resultant matrix.
